channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek Senate Chair Emphasizes Practical Solutions and Concrete Results for All Issues
item.description: Tanzila Narbaeva, Chair of the Uzbek Senate, stressed the need for practical solutions and concrete results on all issues raised in parliament. She stated that vague phrases like "measures are being taken" are insufficient. Clear accountability, timelines, and expected outcomes are required, especially for budget-related matters.

item.title: Strengthening Uzbekistan-Serbia Relations Enhances Cooperation with Europe, Says Senator
item.description: Senator Gulnora Marufova stated that strengthening strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and Serbia, boosted by President Mirziyoyev's visit, is crucial for European cooperation. She highlighted that relations are filled with concrete agreements and joint projects, not just talks, benefiting entrepreneurs and creating jobs.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Bilateral Cooperation with Armenian Prime Minister
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a phone call with Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan to discuss bilateral relations, focusing on trade, economy, and investment. They emphasized developing joint industrial cooperation projects and strengthening connectivity via transport corridors linking Central Asia and the South Caucasus.

item.title: South Korean President invites Central Asian leaders to Seoul for economic cooperation summit
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has invited leaders from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan to a summit in Seoul on September 16. The meeting aims to deepen trade and economic cooperation, strengthen multilateral ties, and advance South Korea's 'New Northern Policy' focused on Eurasia.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes wartime measures: censorship, detention without ID
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a draft law expanding emergency powers, including censorship and detention. Proposals include broader grounds for states of emergency, deployment of armed forces, and designation of the Security Council as the supreme command body.

item.title: Kara-Balta municipal water utility fined for air pollution in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan's Chuy region, the Kara-Balta municipal water utility was fined 28,000 soms for air pollution. A resident's complaint about foul odors from the utility's treatment facilities led to an inspection revealing critical air contamination.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Bilateral Relations with Armenian Prime Minister
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a phone conversation with Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan on September 11. They discussed current issues in developing Uzbek-Armenian relations, particularly in trade, economy, and investment. Both leaders emphasized strengthening regional connectivity through logistics and transport corridors linking Central Asia and the South Caucasus.

item.title: New Tajik Ambassador to Kuwait presents credentials to Amir
item.description: Khusrav Noziri, the new Ambassador of Tajikistan to Kuwait, presented his credentials to the Amir of Kuwait, Sheikh Mishal Ahmad Al-Sabah, on September 8. The Tajik Embassy in Kuwait was also mentioned.

item.title: Tajikistan-Forward business forum to be held in Dushanbe in October 2026
item.description: The 'Tajikistan-Forward' business forum is scheduled to take place in Dushanbe from October 14-15, 2026. Organized by the State Committee for Investments and State Property Management, the event will focus on entrepreneurship, investment, public-private partnerships, venture capital, and innovation.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Armenia to develop new industrial cooperation projects
item.description: Uzbekistan and Armenia will develop new industrial cooperation projects. Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Nikol Pashinyan discussed trade, investment, and the development of transport and logistics corridors in a phone call. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Constitutional Amendments on State of Emergency
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has put draft amendments to constitutional laws on states of emergency and martial law up for public discussion. The country has declared states of emergency multiple times since independence, but never martial law. The first known instance of a state of emergency occurred in June 1990 during inter-ethnic clashes.

item.title: Vietnam's ROX Group May Implement Investment Projects in Uzbekistan
item.description: Vietnam's ROX Group is considering implementing investment projects in Uzbekistan. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev discussed cooperation in energy, geology, finance, and tourism with the company's founder. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Russia to Tighten Controls on Migrants, Medvedev States
item.description: Russia's Security Council Chairman Dmitry Medvedev announced stricter controls on migrants. Those unable to support themselves and their families will have their patents canceled and may be forced to leave Russia. The announcement emphasizes the need for migrants to demonstrate sufficient income.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Inaugurates 15 Projects Remotely
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon remotely inaugurated 15 facilities across Rasht, Nurobod, Sangvor, Lakhsh, and Tajikabad districts. He also reviewed a road project. The inaugurated facilities include community centers, educational buildings, a museum, a hotel, and administrative offices.

item.title: World Bank Outlines Conditions for Financial Aid to Tajikistan
item.description: The World Bank has detailed the conditions for providing financial assistance to Tajikistan. The bank intends to offer up to $1.2 billion in funding to the country. Further details on the proposed financial package are expected.

item.title: Uzbekistan Signs Law Protecting Citizens from Noise Pollution
item.description: Uzbekistan's president has signed a law on protecting citizens from harmful noise effects. The law, passed in October 2025 and approved in June 2026, will take effect three months after official publication. It defines permissible noise levels and establishes quiet hours.

item.title: Central Asian Presidents to Meet South Korean President in Seoul Next Week
item.description: Presidents of Central Asian nations will convene in Seoul next week for the first summit with South Korea. Prior to the summit, a separate meeting will take place between President Lee Jae-myung and the Central Asian presidents.

item.title: Emomali Rahmon Inaugurates Airport, Presidential School, and Museum in Rasht District
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon has inaugurated an airport, a presidential school, and the Nusratullo Maksum museum in the Rasht district. The article indicates further facilities were opened during the president's visit to the region.

item.title: CIS Prepares for "Eurasia-Antiterror – 2026" Counter-Terrorism Exercise
item.description: The CIS Executive Committee reported that practical training for the "Eurasia-Antiterror – 2026" counter-terrorism exercise took place in Minsk. Experts from Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan participated.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee Investigates Compensation for Delayed Domestic Flights
item.description: Uzbekistan's Committee for the Development of Competition is investigating compensation for passengers on domestic flights delayed due to airline fault. The committee noted a significant increase in passenger complaints regarding flight delays and service quality.

item.title: Canada and Ukraine Sign 100-Year Partnership, Agreeing to Drone and Defense Aid
item.description: Canada and Ukraine have signed a 100-year partnership agreement, including the supply of millions of drones to Kyiv. Canada will provide $350 million for air defense and $430 million for gas purchases.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Alter Borders of Zarafshon City and Three Districts
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate approved changes to the borders of Zarafshon city in Navoiy region and Jarqo‘rg‘on and Qiziriq districts in Surxondaryo region. Over 2459 hectares will be incorporated into Zarafshon city for industrial and residential development, aiming to boost investment and create jobs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Spends 1.4 Billion Som on 'Manas Ordo' National Complex Renovation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has allocated 1.4 billion soms from the state budget for the renovation of the 'Manas Ordo' national complex in Talas. President Sadyr Japarov stated the project aims to create a modern museum complex blending heritage and technology, including new facilities for events and digital visitor experiences.

item.title: Tajikistan Inaugurates Presidential School for Gifted Students in Rasht District
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon opened a new Presidential School for gifted students in the Rasht district. The modern facility features 33 classrooms, computer labs with internet access, science labs, vocational training areas, a sports hall, and a canteen, creating jobs for over 60 teachers.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Promises Government Jobs for Akylman Lyceum Graduates
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov announced that graduates of the Akylman Lyceum will be offered government jobs upon completing higher education. He urged students to focus on studies and research, noting that a relevant law is already in effect. Japarov emphasized identifying and nurturing talented children across all regions.

item.title: New Kyrgyz National University Campus Opens in Talas for 3,000 Students
item.description: A new five-story academic building for the Kyrgyz National University's multi-profile institute has opened in Talas, Kyrgyzstan, accommodating 3,000 students. The facility features modern equipment and digital technologies. President Sadyr Japarov attended the opening and urged attention to educational quality and specialist training.

item.title: New Tourist Complex 'Beles-Resort' Opens in Sulyukta, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The tourist complex 'Beles-Resort' has opened in Sulyukta, Batken region, as part of events celebrating Kyrgyzstan's 35th anniversary of independence. Officials stated the complex will enhance tourism in the region, utilize natural beauty, develop domestic tourism, and create new recreational spaces.

item.title: 210 Educational Institutions to Open in Khatlon Region, Tajikistan by 2026
item.description: By 2026, the Khatlon region of Tajikistan plans to open a total of 210 educational institutions, creating 54,674 new study places. This initiative aims to improve learning conditions and address shortages in educational facilities.

item.title: Uzbekistan Receives First C-390 Millennium Military Transport Aircraft
item.description: Brazil's Embraer aviation company has presented the first C-390 Millennium military transport aircraft manufactured for the Uzbek Air Force. Uzbekistan becomes the first C-390 customer in Central Asia. The aircraft is designed for transport, humanitarian missions, and firefighting.

item.title: Environmentalist warns Bishkek faces drinking water shortage risks
item.description: An environmentalist warns Bishkek could face a drinking water shortage if urban development ignores the condition of natural ecosystems and water resources. The city relies on underground sources, and supplying water from elsewhere would be nearly impossible during a severe shortage. Solutions include collecting rainwater and reusing treated wastewater.

item.title: Two killed in Navoi mine incident involving exploding dumper truck tire
item.description: Two people were reportedly killed in a mine in Navoi region when a dumper truck tire exploded. Several other workers sustained injuries of varying degrees. Navoi Mining and Metallurgical Combinat (NMMC) has not yet officially commented on the incident.

item.title: President Emomali Rahmon visits Rasht district for facility openings
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon arrived in the Rasht district for a working visit to open various facilities, meet with residents, and participate in Independence Day celebrations. He inaugurated the reconstructed Rasht district airport, noting its modern conditions for passenger service and future air route restoration.

item.title: Tajikistan and UN Discuss Joint Initiatives for Peace Decade
item.description: Tajikistan's Permanent Representative to the UN met with the High Representative for UNAOC to discuss cooperation. They reviewed the UN General Assembly resolution on the International Decade of Peace (2027-2036) and explored joint initiatives, including a high-level conference to launch the decade and promote a global culture of peace.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia Accelerate Relations After 30 Years of Stagnation
item.description: Despite over 30 years of diplomatic ties, Uzbekistan and Serbia saw little progress until October last year. Recent high-level visits led to numerous agreements, a strategic partnership declaration, and negotiations on free trade and labor migration. Embassies are planned, with the first Uzbek ambassador to Serbia appointed.

item.title: Iran Resumes Ballistic Missile Production Using Existing Components, WSJ Reports
item.description: Iran has resumed ballistic missile production, utilizing stored components and underground facilities, according to The Wall Street Journal. This follows Pentagon chief's February statement that Iran's missile program was "destroyed" by attacks. The report details Iran's continued efforts in missile development.

item.title: Uzbekistan Mandates Immediate Replacement of Defective Goods
item.description: Uzbekistan is introducing a regulation requiring sellers to immediately replace defective goods if an identical product is available. The Senate approved amendments to the Consumer Rights Protection Law. Previously, replacements had a 7-day window, extendable to 20 days if further inspection was needed. Consumers can now participate in quality checks.

item.title: Travel Agency Employees Arrested for Illegally Facilitating Hajj Pilgrimages
item.description: Employees of a travel agency have been arrested for allegedly organizing illegal trips for Hajj. One suspect is the head of a travel agency operating in Kokand, and the other is an employee of a travel agency in Chortoq district. Criminal cases have been initiated against them.

item.title: Iran Temporarily Waives 10% Fee for Fuel Tankers to Revive Oil and Gas Exports
item.description: Iran has temporarily waived a 10% fee for fuel tankers to revive its oil and gas exports, which were disrupted by U.S. maritime blockades. Tehran aims to reduce transport costs and attract foreign vessels to the country through this incentive.

item.title: New Ambassadors from Sweden and Belgium Appointed to Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov received letters of credence from the newly appointed ambassadors of Sweden and Belgium. Martin Rosen is the new Ambassador of Sweden, and Mathias Kende is the new Ambassador of Belgium. The establishment of the Belgian embassy in Tashkent was noted as significant.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan sets presidential election for January 27, 2027 with new rules
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's next presidential election is scheduled for January 27, 2027. The Central Election Commission plans changes to candidate requirements and strategies to combat low voter turnout. Parliament is expected to officially appoint the election date on September 24.
